uncertainObservations: Which hand holds the three swords cannot be settled: the body is seen from behind in a three-quarter turn, so the visible arm on the viewer-right side could be either the figure's left or right arm. Only the forearm and fist are visible; the other arm is hidden under the cloak.

The moon's phase is ambiguous. The entire disc is visible with surface markings across its whole face and no hard terminator, which reads as full, but it is rendered dim and slightly translucent against the stars, so a nearly-full gibbous cannot be excluded.

Whether the standing figure is looking at the two distant walking figures, at the ground swords, or simply downward at the pavement cannot be determined; the head is in profile, tilted down, with the eye barely resolvable.

There is a small bright disc with a faint circular halo high in the sky near the top centre-right. I could not tell whether it is a second small moon/planet or just a bright star with a lens-halo; it reads more like a haloed star.
Whether the low sun at the horizon is setting or rising is not determinable from the image.
The two distant figures appear unarmed, but their hands and any belt-hung weapons are too small and too dark to confirm; I cannot rule out something carried at their sides.
The number of concentric rings in both the pavement engraving and the sky diagram is not countable, nor are the glyphs along the pavement's outer band legible.
Whether the standing figure's three blades splay apart or merely overlap in perspective is hard to judge; three guards and three pommels are nevertheless clearly separate.

Whether the dark object on the lower terrace to the viewer-left of the walking figures is a bollard, a lamp post or a third small figure could not be resolved; it is small and silhouetted, and I did not count it as a figure.
